data.critique: Do not approve yet. The NSC vote favours Protein degradation (3/4 wells), but each is a single replicate, with only modest MG-132-similarity (0.64-0.71), while the 10 µM well is a strong Microtubule-stabilizer match (0.895) and the first k-NN atlas was 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers. The final k-NN list is also split with DNA replication/damage. Morphology reports are explicitly non-specific and unreliable versus the out-of-focus DMSO: no mitotic increase, no clear microtubule bundling at ≤1 µM, and the enlarged, high-integrated-DNA nuclei could fit DNA replication/damage, not Protein degradation specifically. 0.60 is therefore over-calibrated. One affordable, discriminating test exists: run the free phenotype description on the already-acquired 3 µM well w_dddcf8dd41 (dose index 6, rep 1), specifically scoring microtubule bundle/spindle formation versus an intact tubulin network and the nuclear phenotype. That well sits at the tubulin-contrast transition (-1.11 at 0.1 µM, +2.94 at 3 µM, +30.4 at 10 µM) and was acquired for this purpose but never visually inspected. Absence of bundling/mitotic arrest would support rejecting the stabilizer runner-up; clear bundling would reverse the call. Until then the Protein degradation conclusion is not secure.

data.note:
Specimen correctly called as Protein degradation (proteasome inhibitor I, CID 16760625, BBBC021 annotates as Protein degradation). Cellular profile — enlarged, elongated nuclei with increased integrated DNA but decreased mean DNA intensity, preserved/intensified tubulin — matched MG-132-like proteasome inhibition rather than microtubule stabilizer bundling, though the 10 µM tubulin-contrast spike required careful dose discrimination.

Literature context: MG132 mechanisms are reviewed in PMID 41631982 and PMID 22897979 (proteasome inhibitor induces apoptosis / anticancer activity), consistent with proteasome-dependent cell-cycle effects observed here.

Note: ChEMBL has no curated mechanism for this specific compound; call was supported by NSC atlas and PubChem identity.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth is Protein degradation (proteasome inhibitor I, CID 16760625, name and BBBC021 structure agree e22/e23) - my submitted conclusion of Protein degradation was correct on both attempts (p=0.60 then p=0.48). Literature found in this run is consistent that MG132 is the prototypical proteasome inhibitor used to define this class PMID 41631982 and that it induces apoptosis via proteasome inhibition PMID 22897979.

What got right: The core signal was the consistency of the nuclear phenotype across the non-toxic range and the NSC vote stability when multiple doses were included. Wells w_0e5c8b0c20 at 1uM e3 (nuc_eccentricity z=+11.8, nuc_dna_mean z=-7.6), w_2d09ed9d0f at 0.1uM e4 (+8.7, -7.1, area +5.9), and w_dddcf8dd41 at 3uM e13 (+10.5, -7.2, tub_mean +7.6) all showed the same high-eccentricity / low DNA-mean pattern. NSC vote went from 2/3 e5 to 3/4 Protein degradation e14 when the 3uM intermediate was added, while k-NN shifted away from Microtubule stabilizers. I correctly weighted that 3-dose replication (e5,e14,e3,e4,e13) over a single well, and used dose_response trends to de-prioritize the runner-up: frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.77 e16 and frac_large_nucleus rho=-1.00 e15 contradict microtubule stabilizer / Aurora expectation which should increase mitotic fraction and polyploidy with dose, and describe_phenotype e8 reported no mitotic increase and no clear bundling at <=1uM.

What misled / what I missed: The 10uM well w_d128269dd7 e2 was the main distractor: tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean +11.3, tub_std +9.7 with dose-response rho=+1.00 p=0 e9. That drove the first compare_to_reference_atlas e5 to k-neighbour 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers despite NSC 2/3 Protein degradation, and the review correctly flagged the strong 0.895 Microtubule-stabilizer match at 10uM at only modest 0.64-0.71 MG-132 similarity for the other wells. My hypothesis update e17 kept Microtubule stabilizers at 0.25 for this reason (e2, e6, e5). After the PI-requested describe_phenotype on the transition well w_dddcf8dd41 e19 (3uM, where tub contrast was +2.94 vs -1.11 at 0.1uM and +30.4 at 10uM), the microscopist returned candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, Microtubule stabilizers with bundle-like tubulin - intermediate between DMSO and 10uM. That plus the split second k-NN (DNA replication 4/10, DNA damage 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10 e14) forced me to lower confidence to 0.48 e20, citing e19, e9, e2 as contradicting Protein degradation.

Why: Acquisition choice to sample the extreme high dose (10uM, 198 cells, density lower e6) imported toxicity/secondarily stabilized tubulin texture into the atlas comparison without replication; with only single replicate per dose and 2 fields per microscopy vs out-of-focus DMSO (e6-e8 "unknown"/"none", density reports inconsistent), visual calls were explicitly non-specific and could be driven by cell loss e12 rho=-1.00 for cell_count. I did not over-calibrate to 0.60 - rationale "only toxic 10uM flips" was correct but similarity scores were modest, so 0.48 better reflected split atlas and intermediate bundling that supports but does not confirm reject of stabilizer. Search_literature e24-e25 after unblinding confirmed no curated ChEMBL mechanism and no direct support for proteasome-inhibition enlarged-nuclei vs replication/damage, which explains why k-NN DNA replication/damage persisted as a confounder.

No clinical implications are inferred; this is screening morphology only. Next discriminating test as submitted remains proteasome activity (Suc-LLVY-AMC) / ubiquitin/p21 WB + phospho-H3/DNA-content flow and acetyl-tubulin IF on same 0.1-10uM series vs MG-132/docetaxel controls.

Correctly down-weighted 10uM toxic well after acquiring dose series and re-checking atlas e14, with visual e7-e8 showing no mitotic arrest at <=1uM

## Reflection

Unblinded truth is Protein degradation (proteasome inhibitor I, CID 16760625, name and BBBC021 structure agree e22/e23) - my submitted conclusion of Protein degradation was correct on both attempts (p=0.60 then p=0.48). Literature found in this run is consistent that MG132 is the prototypical proteasome inhibitor used to define this class PMID 41631982 and that it induces apoptosis via proteasome inhibition PMID 22897979.

What got right: The core signal was the consistency of the nuclear phenotype across the non-toxic range and the NSC vote stability when multiple doses were included. Wells w_0e5c8b0c20 at 1uM e3 (nuc_eccentricity z=+11.8, nuc_dna_mean z=-7.6), w_2d09ed9d0f at 0.1uM e4 (+8.7, -7.1, area +5.9), and w_dddcf8dd41 at 3uM e13 (+10.5, -7.2, tub_mean +7.6) all showed the same high-eccentricity / low DNA-mean pattern. NSC vote went from 2/3 e5 to 3/4 Protein degradation e14 when the 3uM intermediate was added, while k-NN shifted away from Microtubule stabilizers. I correctly weighted that 3-dose replication (e5,e14,e3,e4,e13) over a single well, and used dose_response trends to de-prioritize the runner-up: frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.77 e16 and frac_large_nucleus rho=-1.00 e15 contradict microtubule stabilizer / Aurora expectation which should increase mitotic fraction and polyploidy with dose, and describe_phenotype e8 reported no mitotic increase and no clear bundling at <=1uM.

What misled / what I missed: The 10uM well w_d128269dd7 e2 was the main distractor: tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean +11.3, tub_std +9.7 with dose-response rho=+1.00 p=0 e9. That drove the first compare_to_reference_atlas e5 to k-neighbour 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers despite NSC 2/3 Protein degradation, and the review correctly flagged the strong 0.895 Microtubule-stabilizer match at 10uM at only modest 0.64-0.71 MG-132 similarity for the other wells. My hypothesis update e17 kept Microtubule stabilizers at 0.25 for this reason (e2, e6, e5). After the PI-requested describe_phenotype on the transition well w_dddcf8dd41 e19 (3uM, where tub contrast was +2.94 vs -1.11 at 0.1uM and +30.4 at 10uM), the microscopist returned candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, Microtubule stabilizers with bundle-like tubulin - intermediate between DMSO and 10uM. That plus the split second k-NN (DNA replication 4/10, DNA damage 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10 e14) forced me to lower confidence to 0.48 e20, citing e19, e9, e2 as contradicting Protein degradation.

Why: Acquisition choice to sample the extreme high dose (10uM, 198 cells, density lower e6) imported toxicity/secondarily stabilized tubulin texture into the atlas comparison without replication; with only single replicate per dose and 2 fields per microscopy vs out-of-focus DMSO (e6-e8 "unknown"/"none", density reports inconsistent), visual calls were explicitly non-specific and could be driven by cell loss e12 rho=-1.00 for cell_count. I did not over-calibrate to 0.60 - rationale "only toxic 10uM flips" was correct but similarity scores were modest, so 0.48 better reflected split atlas and intermediate bundling that supports but does not confirm reject of stabilizer. Search_literature e24-e25 after unblinding confirmed no curated ChEMBL mechanism and no direct support for proteasome-inhibition enlarged-nuclei vs replication/damage, which explains why k-NN DNA replication/damage persisted as a confounder.

No clinical implications are inferred; this is screening morphology only. Next discriminating test as submitted remains proteasome activity (Suc-LLVY-AMC) / ubiquitin/p21 WB + phospho-H3/DNA-content flow and acetyl-tubulin IF on same 0.1-10uM series vs MG-132/docetaxel controls.

What was right:
- NSC vote 3/4 Protein degradation e14 replicated across 1uM e3, 0.1uM e4, 3uM e13 - supported 0.60/0.48 call over single-well k-NN
- Used negative mitotic/polyploidy dose trends e16 rho=-0.77, e15 rho=-1.00 to contradict Microtubule stabilizer expectation despite e2 tub_glcm_contrast +30.4 and e5 8/10 k-NN
- Correctly down-weighted 10uM toxic well after acquiring dose series and re-checking atlas e14, with visual e7-e8 showing no mitotic arrest at <=1uM

What was wrong or missed:
- Initial k-NN 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers e5 and e2 extreme tub texture misled to retain 0.25 stabilizer probability e17
- PI-requested 3uM visual e19 reporting bundle-like tubulin / Aurora candidates introduced uncertainty and split k-NN DNA replication 4/10 e14 - caused confidence drop 0.60->0.48
- Relied on single replicate per dose with modest similarities 0.64-0.71 and 2-field out-of-focus DMSO microscopy e6-e8, over-calibrated at first submission

Proposed next experiment: Proteasome Suc-LLVY-AMC + ubiquitin/p21 WB and phospho-H3/DNA-content flow with acetyl-tubulin IF on 0.1-10uM 24h series vs MG-132/docetaxel/camptothecin controls to separate primary proteasome inhibition from secondary tubulin stabilization at 10uM.
